first.rationale: Competitor entry pricing creates an immediate, segment-specific threat to price-sensitive SMB acquisition, and prior evidence indicates targeted promotional pricing lifted both acquisition and revenue in this segment. I will verify the original pricing record for durability, qualification, and post-promotion retention effects, while verifying onboarding evidence because declining completion and activation may make an onboarding intervention the higher-sustainability alternative. Any pricing test should be narrowly targeted and guarded against low-quality or discount-dependent revenue.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. The verified prior result increased completion by 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and improved 30-day retention by 3%, directly addressing both current onboarding-completion and activation declines while supporting durable qualified revenue. Do not use promotional pricing: its verified 40% discount increased qualified revenue short term but reduced 30-day retention by 12%, making it unsuitable for the primary objective despite competitive price pressure.
